title: Choose the visual world — Christian Waldo homepage
question: The roll assigned The Tape Vault. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Your light blue / white / grey pin binds every card.

options.label: The Tape Vault
options.lineage: studio tape libraries: reel boxes, typed spine labels, shelf index cards
options.thesis: Every project is a reel on the shelf, so the page is the vault you walk instead of a headline with a waveform under it.
options.viewport: One shelf run of reel boxes head-on, edge to edge, spines typed with project names; the shelf index card top-left carries the name and what he does; the last slot on the run is an empty label reading START A PROJECT, and it is the primary action.
options.risk: Reads as archive nostalgia if the boxes stay pictures instead of behaving like objects you pull.

raised.raise: Three materials only — board, label, ink — and controls take no colour: they are punched, embossed or scored, never a tinted button.
No midtone anywhere: every edge is lit or unlit, hard, with no soft shadow doing the work a line should do.
One reserved brightest value, the chinagraph blue, spent only on the element under attention.
Attention is the state model: the box you are on comes forward and its label reads full strength, with afterglow on the way back.

options.label: The Session Take Sheet
options.lineage: recording-session take sheets and track sheets, filled by hand
options.thesis: The page is the document a session actually produces: ruled columns, takes logged in pencil, the keeper circled in blue.
options.viewport: A single ruled sheet filling the viewport, header block with name and services typed in the boxes, the portfolio as logged takes down the column, the inquiry line the one row left blank.
options.risk: Also the direction a careful run in this category lands on: paper grid, pencil, quietly tasteful.

options.label: Step Row
options.lineage: early-80s rhythm machine step row under a running chase light
options.thesis: The catalogue is sixteen steps and a chase light: the page keeps time while you read it.
options.viewport: One unbroken sixteen-step row across the first screen, each step a project, the chase light sweeping it, the tempo readout replaced by what he does.
options.case: Wins audience identification outright — every artist knows this row by heart — and loses product clarity: a step row sells a loop, not a producer you hand a record to.
options.risk: Translated to light blue the keys lose the candy-colour quartering the world is recognised by.

options.label: Kiosk Print
options.lineage: state kiosk goods printed in three permitted inks, slightly off-register
options.thesis: Production, mixing, mastering and commissions as four printed goods from one office, one restricted ink set, one mark each.
options.viewport: A kiosk grid of printed goods filling the screen, each cell a service or a release with its own office mark, the inquiry cell taking the third ink.
options.case: Holds product clarity — four services read as four goods in a scannable grid — and loses audience identification: state ephemera is not the artist's world.
options.risk: Without strict register discipline the grid flattens into ordinary cards.

options.label: Weimar Cabaret Bill
options.lineage: berlin cabaret bill in two harsh inks
options.thesis: The roster as one evening's programme, ranked and leaning off the vertical.
options.viewport: A black field with an angular figure cut from it and the programme stepping down the column.
options.case: Loses both axes: a producer's roster is not an ordered evening, and the two-ink field fights the pinned palette rather than translating into it.
options.kept: No midtone — lit or unlit, hard edges only.
options.risk: Nostalgic theatre over a working offer.

options.label: Depot Destination Blind
options.lineage: dyed duck-cloth destination blind stepping under one window
options.thesis: The catalogue as courses of cloth stepping under a fixed window.
options.viewport: One lit window with a course of cloth halted mid-step behind it.
options.case: Loses both axes: the depot has no hold on an artist choosing a producer, and one window at a time starves a portfolio that must be scanned.
options.kept: Three materials only, and controls that take no colour — punch, stitch and relief instead.
options.risk: Beautiful and mute; the offer never gets a second surface.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.lineage: sunlight diffracted through a cloud's droplet edge
options.thesis: Quiet achromatic field with spectral colour only at the edges.
options.viewport: Wide white margins, slate body text, a narrow colour fringe at one edge.
options.case: Loses both axes: no artist identifies with atmospheric optics, and a page whose colour lives in hairlines cannot carry an offer at page scale.
options.kept: One reserved brightest value, spent only on the element under attention.
options.risk: Lands as the neutral template with a tinted edge.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.lineage: alien forest understory lit by spore glow at nightfall
options.thesis: The page lights itself two steps ahead of the visitor.
options.viewport: Near-black ground with labels blooming beside glowing growths, no fixed grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is the near-black-plus-neon page this category already ships, and a gridless glow field hides the services and the action.
options.kept: Attention as the state model — what you are on comes forward, with afterglow on the way back.
options.risk: The genre default wearing a forest.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What a producer site ships: portrait hero, play buttons, three service cards, a contact form — executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Full-width portrait with the name over it, a row of three service cards below, a blue primary button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other producer site by design — which is sometimes exactly what a client wants.
